title: Pharmacy transmission of monitoring program data and the dispenser guide's reporting requirements
subtopic: Pharmacy transmission and the dispenser guide
rule_summary: Under 105 CMR 700.012(A)(1) a pharmacy to which the reporting requirement of 105 CMR 700.012 applies shall, in accordance with standards established by the Commissioner, transmit to the Department or its agent the pharmacy identifier, customer identification number and associated information as specified in the PMP Dispensing Guide issued by the Commissioner. Section 1, Reporting Requirements, of the Massachusetts Prescription Monitoring Program Data Submission Guide for Dispensers (Version 5.2, May 2023) states that pharmacies are required to submit dispensing information on federally controlled substances in Schedules II through V and gabapentin, a Massachusetts Schedule VI substance, through the PMP Clearinghouse application; that the reporting requirements apply to all pharmacies registered with the Massachusetts Board of Pharmacy and to all pharmacies in health facilities registered with the Massachusetts Department of Public Health that dispense federally controlled substances in Schedules II through V and gabapentin; and that they apply to any pharmacy located in another state, commonwealth, district or territory that delivers a prescription in Schedules II through V and gabapentin to a person located in Massachusetts, including, but not limited to, mail-order pharmacies.
exam_relevance: Tests what a reporting pharmacy transmits, that the dispenser guide names gabapentin alongside federally controlled substances in Schedules II through V, and which pharmacies the guide says the requirements reach.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations
Massachusetts Prescription Monitoring Program Data Submission Guide for Dispensers, Version 5.2 (May 2023)

common_confusions: Treating gabapentin's reporting as a change to its federal status, when the guide lists it apart from the federally controlled substances in Schedules II through V and describes it as a Massachusetts Schedule VI substance.
Assuming every Massachusetts Schedule VI drug is reported because gabapentin is.
Treating the transmission as a duty of the individual pharmacist, when 105 CMR 700.012(A)(1) places it on the pharmacy.
verification_notes: 105 CMR 700.012(A)(1) read verbatim in the current Department of Public Health publication of 105 CMR 700.000 on mass.gov, and section 1 of the Data Submission Guide for Dispensers read in the Version 5.2 document served at the cited mass.gov address, both on 2026-09-14.
